source.title_on_document: LLM Randomness and Creativity: An Experiment on Human-AI Collaboration

supplement.holds: The paper mentions no supplement or online appendix. DAT regression results are not reported anywhere (p. 1772: 'for the DAT, no coefficients were significant, so we do not report them').

paper_design_summary: Online experiment on Prolific (December 2025) with a 3 x 3 between-subjects design: participants were randomly assigned to one task (Remote Associates Test, Alternate Uses Test, or Divergent Association Task) and to one AI condition (no AI, an LLM assistant at temperature 0.1, or an LLM assistant at temperature 1.2), and completed three rounds of the task. AUT and DAT outputs were scored by the mean and maximum pairwise semantic distance among each participant's own responses (spaCy embeddings); RAT was scored by accuracy. AI use was optional, and only 48.7 percent of participants with access used it.

studies.label: 3 x 3 between-subjects experiment (task x LLM randomness), Prolific

participants.exclusions: 960 participants were recruited; those who did not complete the study or failed an attention check were excluded, leaving 775. The paper does not say how many of the 185 excluded had been randomized (randomization happens mid-survey, after the verbal fluency task). Arm Ns in Table I sum to 775 (AUT 213, DAT 245, RAT 317). A separate pilot of 40 Prolific participants is not part of the analysis.
participants.who: Prolific participants paid $2.20; 48.4 percent female, mean age 41.89 (SD 12.40)
participants.quote: We then proceeded to recruit 960 participants (also from Prolific but different from those included in the pilot) and paid them $2.20 to complete the study. After excluding participants that did not complete the study or failed an attention check, we were left with 775 participants
participants.locator: p. 1772 (PDF p. 3), Section III.D Participants; arm Ns in p. 1773 (PDF p. 4), Table I

ai_tool.name_model: not_stated (an LLM assistant with temperature set to 0.1 or 1.2)
ai_tool.how_used: A chat panel beside the task ('I'm here to help if you need suggestions or want to brainstorm ideas. Just type your question below.'); use was optional. Among participants with access, 48.7 percent (251 of 519) used it; non-use was 40.0 percent (58/145) for AUT, 55.7 percent (118/212) for RAT, and 56.8 percent (92/162) for DAT (p. 1772). Telemetry logged interactions and the share of AI-generated words incorporated into responses.

task.description: Each participant did one of three tasks for three rounds: the Alternate Uses Test (creative uses of an object, at least 3 ideas per round), the Divergent Association Task (10 words as unrelated as possible), or the Remote Associates Test (find the word linking three cue words; convergent thinking).
task.duration: Three rounds; total time not stated. Participants were paid $2.20.

outcomes.name: AUT average semantic distance
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: spaCy en_core_web_md 300-dimensional word embeddings; for each participant's set of AUT responses, mean of all pairwise cosine distances (1 - similarity). Variety among one participant's own responses, so coded flexibility rather than diversity. Codebook's automated_score ('semantic-distance scoring of divergent-thinking tests') could also apply.

eligibility.reason: People were randomly assigned to no AI, a low-temperature LLM, or a high-temperature LLM (crossed with task); 775 analyzed overall, with 213 (AUT), 245 (DAT), and 317 (RAT) per task, all above 50. AUT and DAT outputs are scored by computed semantic distance and RAT by accuracy. AI use was optional (48.7 percent of those with access used it), so AI-vs-no-AI contrasts are intention-to-treat on availability; regressions also control for self-selected AI_used.

one_line_finding: LLM temperature (1.2 vs 0.1) and AI availability did not change AUT semantic distance (HighRandomness -0.008, SE 0.037; NoAI -0.002, SE 0.044; Table II, p. 1773) or RAT accuracy in regressions (Table III, p. 1774), though the text reports AI availability raised RAT accuracy from 45 to 55 percent (p < .05, p. 1772).
open_questions: Table II and III regressions control for AI_used, a post-assignment, self-selected variable; the NoAI coefficients are therefore not clean intention-to-treat contrasts. The only unconditional AI-vs-no-AI comparison is the RAT 45 vs 55 percent in the Discussion, with p only.
Regression N and whether the unit is the participant or the participant-round are not printed.

Whether the AUT/DAT within-participant semantic distance should be coded flexibility (codebook rule on variety among one person's ideas) or overall_creativity / automated_score (standard DAT scoring).
Whether RAT accuracy (convergent) belongs beside rated creativity (codebook open question).
Holm adjustment is stated for 'this and all following results' starting with the outcome-satisfaction comparison; unclear whether Table II/III stars are adjusted.
notes: Single 6-page proceedings paper; all tables (I to III) and Figure 1 read on the PDF. Table I reports only self-reported constructs (AI attitude, process and outcome satisfaction, perceived effort, ownership, motivation) by cell, plus cell Ns; these self-report outcomes and the Table II/III satisfaction, ownership, and intrinsic motivation regressions are not listed as outcomes because they are not scored on the output. Self-reported creativity was also collected before and after the task. The LLM model is not named. Country of participants not stated. The paper cites Kumar et al. (2025) as related work but analyzes its own new sample.
